chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, and others, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He said: 'Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) passed away and left sixty male slaves, so he emancipated a third of them. So I drew lots among them, and selected twenty, and I emancipated them.'
ai.seo_question: How did the Imams handle the emancipation of slaves in their wills?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (as) illustrates the practical application of bequests (wasiyyah) within the Ahl al-Bayt, highlighting their generosity and adherence to Islamic law regarding the emancipation of slaves. The specific detail of drawing lots (qur'a) to select the freed slaves from the remaining two-thirds underscores the precision and fairness with which the Imams managed their estates, ensuring that the act of manumission was both a spiritual merit and a structured legal obligation. This practice serves as a model for Shia jurisprudence on the distribution of wealth and the status of slaves in early Islamic society.

en.hubeali:
Humayd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Ja’far Bin Sama’at, and someone else, from Aban, from Muhammad Bin Marwan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> passed away and left (as legacy) sixty slaves, so he<sup>asws</sup> emancipated (freed) a third of them. So I<sup>asws</sup> drew lots between them, so I<sup>asws</sup> brought out twenty and freed them’.
en.sarwar: 12. Flumayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah, from Ja‘far ibn Sama‘ah and from more than one person from Aban from Muhammad ibn Marwan who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, died and left sixty slaves, of whom he set free one-third. I picked up the ones to be free by means of casting a raffle.’”
